messages.author: 3713f8b66ab2ca1d
messages.subject: sparse data in logreg
parts:
Dear group members,

I have something like a fundamental question about logreg on corpus data. I have read that logistic regression is very sensitive, among other things, to sparse data. Now on corpus data sparseness is likely to occur. But if my coefficients and standard errors look "normal" do I have to care about that?

Best,
Anne

messages.author: 3edc58ee737edd94
messages.subject: Re: [StatForLing with R] sparse data in logreg
parts:
Well,

- any regression, any statistic becomes less reliable with sparse data;
- just to clarify, what do you mean, a coefficient and/or a standard error "look normal"?

messages.subject: Re: [StatForLing with R] sparse data in logreg
parts: Well, the superset the data, the more important the regression diagnostics become, such as influential observations (using dffits and dfbetas). I'd apart from the usual checks one should do (in particular protecting against overfitting), these don't give cause for concern, you may be safe-ish.
